correctness.rationale: For a specified cyclic k-set, the cyclic permutation and rooted forest count gives k!·k·n^{n−k−1}, also n! when k=n. Thus p(k)=(k/n)Q_{n,k}, with conditionally uniform labels. The log-product estimate on bounded k/√n ranges and a Gaussian tail bound give the Rayleigh limit. For the Cox claim, expand the conditional Laplace functional for any nonnegative continuous compactly supported f in elementary symmetric sums of b_v=1−exp(−f(v/√n)), weighted in order ℓ by (k)_ℓ/(n)_ℓ. On bounded k/√n ranges the absolute terms are bounded by C^ℓ/ℓ!; Riemann sums and omission of repeated indices give exp(−r∫(1−exp(−f))) for k/√n→r, including r=0. Mixing then gives the asserted vague limit. The conditional no-hit probability is hypergeometric, giving E exp(−tR), and scaling the Rayleigh integral shows the t^{−2} tail. Independently, the k+1 gaps around the ordered sample are a uniform weak composition of n−k; M−1 is the first gap. Weighting that gap j by s!·binom(j+s,s) gives s!·binom(n+s,k+s)/binom(n,k) by convolution, the claimed conditional rising moment even when k=n or s>n. The mean follows by Gaussian Riemann summation. For s=2, the sum of kQ_{n,k}/[(k+1)(k+2)] up to √n differs from the harmonic sum by O(1) using 1−Q≤k(k−1)/(2n); the tail contributes O(1). The prefactor is 2n+O(1), so the variance has coefficient one. For s>2, fixed-k dominated convergence is justified by k^{1−s}; summing via the beta integral yields s/[(s−1)(s−2)]. Lower-order terms in the rising polynomial have strictly smaller scale, including n log n for order two.
residual_risks: The finite checks corroborate exact identities only; the bounds and limits were checked analytically. The higher-moment statement fixes an integer order before n tends to infinity; no uniformity or point-process error rate is asserted.

evidence: The exact count law combined with a uniform k-subset gives the finite negative-hypergeometric law. The typical k≈√n scale determines the Cox limit by a standard conditional sampling argument. The variance needs the full logarithmic range k≤√n, and the moments of order greater than two are controlled by the fixed-k probabilities of order 1/n.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The point-process step is a standard but explicit consequence of more than the count limit. The weak Rayleigh limit alone does not control rare cores: the second and higher finite moments need the exact low-k weights, a uniform tail estimate and a distinct asymptotic analysis. The comparison work did not locate a stronger label-order theorem supplying those conclusions.

value.rationale: The earliest cyclic vertex in a deterministic ordering is a natural statistic for scanning a random functional graph. The result separates the typical √n label scale from a finite variance dominated by a logarithmic range of core sizes and higher moments dominated by rare small cores. The coefficient of the logarithm and the full fixed-integer moment constants quantify this distinction; neither reporting a weak limit alone nor restating the cyclic-core distribution does so.
residual_risks: Scope is uniform random self-maps and this particular ordered statistic, not exchangeable in-degree models in general.
